leadText: The following is a list of all of the English language home video releases of the Pokémon movies in and . DVD releases are for , releases are for (although they may be playable in other regions), and all releases are .
plainText:
The following is a list of all of the English language home video releases of the Pokémon movies in and . DVD releases are for , releases are for (although they may be playable in other regions), and all releases are .

==Single movie releases==
===Mewtwo Strikes Back===
Mewtwo Strikes Back was released by on home video in the United States. Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Pikachu's Vacation. The promotional card was included in early releases of both the VHS and the DVD.

It was released on VHS in the United States on March 21, 2000 with the catalogue number 18020. It was released on DVD in the United States on March 21, 2000 with the catalogue number 18020. These releases use a 4:3 . The VHS had The Story of Mewtwo's Origin (first two minutes of The Uncut Story of Mewtwo's Origin) added to the beginning of the movie and includes a preview for The Power of One. The DVD has English audio, with optional English and French closed captions. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Commentary audio track by Director Michael Haigney and Producer Norman J. Grossfeld
The Story of Mewtwo's Origin (first two minutes of The Uncut Story of Mewtwo's Origin)
Music video for 's " " (the movie's ending theme)
Theatrical trailer of the movie
Preview of The Power of One
"Ash's journey"
DVD-ROM features: Pokémon fun facts, history of , history of the video games, Pokémon Web World, Nintendo game guides, special events page, Pokémon webcards, Poké-patterns, Pokémon posters and more

It was re-released on in the United States on April 26, 2005 by Warner Bros. The movie including Pikachu's Vacation is split between two MiniDVDs. And also includes the following extras on the second disc:
Music video for 's " " (the movie's ending theme)
"Ash's Journey" introduction video
The Story of Mewtwo's Origin (first two minutes of The Uncut Story of Mewtwo's Origin)

It was re-released on DVD in the United States on February 2, 2016 by , with distribution through . This re-release does not include a Pikachu short or the other special features. This release uses a aspect ratio. However, for some strange reason, there are no opening credits except for the film's main title reveal.

 

===The Power of One===
The Power of One was released by on home video in the United States. Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Pikachu's Rescue Adventure. The promotional card was included in early releases of both the VHS and the DVD.

It was released on VHS in the United States on November 14, 2000 with the catalogue number 18620. It was released on DVD in the United States on November 14, 2000 with the catalogue number 18620. These releases use a 4:3 . The VHS includes a preview for Spell of the Unown: Entei. The DVD has English and Quebec French audio, and English and French closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Musical performances from the Pokémon the Movie 2000 soundtrack
"They Don't Understand" by 
"Story Of" and performance by Alysha Antonino
"Pokémon World" by featuring 
Making of the soundtrack
Theatrical trailer of the movie
Theatrical trailer of Spell of the Unown: Entei

It was re-released on DVD in the United States on February 2, 2016 by with distribution through . This re-release does not include a Pikachu short or the other special features. This release uses a aspect ratio.

 

===Spell of the Unown: Entei===
Spell of the Unown: Entei was released by on home video in the United States. Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Pikachu & Pichu. The promotional card was included in early releases of both the VHS and the DVD.

It was released on VHS in the United States on August 21, 2001 with the catalogue number 21251. It was released on DVD in the United States on August 21, 2001 with the catalogue number 21251. These releases use a 4:3 . The DVD has English and French audio, and English and French closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Pokérap GS (Johto Pokérap)
Making of "To Know the Unknown"
What the Filmmakers Say (Commentary audio track)
Theatrical trailer of the movie
Japanese trailer for Celebi: The Voice of the Forest
Little Known Unown Facts!

It was re-released on DVD in the United States on February 2, 2016 published by and distributed by Warner Bros. This re-release does not include a Pikachu short or the other special features. This release uses a aspect ratio.

 

===Celebi: The Voice of the Forest===
 
Celebi: The Voice of the Forest was released on home video in the United States by and in Canada by . Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Pikachu's PikaBoo. The promotional card was included in early releases of both the VHS and the DVD.

It was released on VHS in the United States on March 18, 2003 with the catalogue number 29173. It was released on DVD in the United States by on March 18, 2003 with the catalogue number 29124. It was released on DVD in Canada by Alliance Atlantis with the catalogue number 4611. They all use a 4:3 . The DVD has English audio, with optional English closed captions. In addition to Pikachu's PikaBoo, the DVD release includes the following extras:
Audio commentary by the actors and producers,
Multi-angle animation progression on four scenes
A trivia game
A Trading Card Game tutorial as a DVD-ROM feature
Theatrical trailers (domestic and Japanese trailer)
A sneak peek at the next Pokémon movie

It was re-released on DVD in the United States on April 26, 2011 by . The re-release of this movie does not include a Pikachu short or other special features. This release uses a aspect ratio.

It was re-released again on DVD in the United States on October 7, 2014 by . This re-release does not include a Pikachu short, other special features, or closed captioning, despite advertising those features on the back cover. This release uses a aspect ratio. 

On September 22, 2020, the film was once again re-released on DVD (under catalog number 2130815) in the United States by following ' 49% acquisition of Miramax. Similar to the 2011 and 2014 releases, this release does not include the Pikachu short, any special features, or closed captioning, other than being presented in aspect ratio. 

 

===Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias===
 
Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias was released on home video by in the United States. Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Camp Pikachu. The promotional cards and were included in early releases of the DVD.

It was released on VHS in the United States on January 20, 2004 with the catalogue number 32758. It was released on DVD in the United States by Miramax on January 20, 2004 with the catalogue number 32733. These releases were distributed by and use a 4:3 . The DVD has English and French audio, with optional English closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Sneak peeks of six other non-Pokémon movies
Location scouting in Venice
An animation stages feature (Water Chariot Race, Race Spectators, Crowd on a Bridge, Latias, Defense Mechanism of Alltomare, Wave)
The characters of the movie
Pokémon Heroes trivia game

It was re-released on DVD in the United States on April 12, 2011 distributed by . The re-release of this movie does not include a Pikachu short or the other special features. This release uses a 4:3 , despite advertising a aspect ratio..

It was re-released again on DVD in the United States on October 7, 2014 distributed by . This re-release does not include a Pikachu short, the other special features, or subtitles, despite advertising those features on the back cover. This release uses a 4:3 , despite advertising a aspect ratio.

On September 22, 2020, the film was re-released on DVD (under catalog number 2130692) once again in the United States by following ' 49% acquisition of Miramax. Similar to the Echo Bridge and Lionsgate releases, this releases does not feature a Pikachu short, any special features or subtitles and is presented in aspect ratio. On this release however it does not falsely advertise that special features or subtitles or a Pikachu short were included unlike the previous re-releases. 

 

===Jirachi: Wish Maker===
 
Jirachi: Wish Maker was released on home video by in the United States. Both the VHS and DVD release include the Pikachu short Gotta Dance!. The promotional card was included in early releases of both the VHS and the DVD.

It was released on VHS in the United States on June 1, 2004 with the catalogue number 36331. It was released on DVD in the United States by Miramax on June 1, 2004 with the catalogue number 36330. These releases were distributed by and use a 4:3 . The DVD includes English closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Sneak peaks of five other non-Pokémon movies
Trivia game
"Make a Wish" Music Video
Message from the director, Mr. Yuyama
Pokémon character artwork and bios
Jirachi Wish Maker original artwork

It was re-released on DVD in the United States on May 3, 2011 by . The re-release of this movie does not include a Pikachu short or the other special features. This release uses a 4:3 , despite advertising a aspect ratio.

It was re-released again on DVD in the United States on October 7, 2014 by . This re-release does not include the Pikachu short, other special features, or subtitles, despite advertising them on the back cover. This release uses a 16:9 .

On September 22, 2020, the film was once again re-released on DVD (under catalog number 2130696) in the United States by following ' 49% acquisition of Miramax. Similar to the Echo Bridge and Lionsgate releases, this release does not feature a Pikachu short, any special features, or subtitles and is presented in aspect ratio. On this release however, it does not falsely advertise that special features or subtitles or a Pikachu short were included, unlike the previous re-releases. 

 

===Destiny Deoxys===
 
Destiny Deoxys was released on home video by in the United States. The promotional card was included in early releases of the VHS and DVD.

It was released on VHS and DVD in the United States by Miramax on February 15, 2005 with the catalogue number 38833. These releases were distributed by and use a 4:3 . The DVD has English and French audio, with optional English closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Sneak peaks of seven other non-Pokémon movies
Gallery: poster art from the Japanese movie
Who's That Pokémon?, meet the new Pokémon from the movie (still images)
"On Location with the Director"
"Be a Poké-Quiz Whiz!"

It was re-released on DVD in the United States on May 3, 2011 by . This re-release does not include the special features. This release uses a aspect ratio.

It was re-released again on DVD in the United States on October 7, 2014 by . This re-release does not include the special features or subtitles, despite advertising those features on the back cover. This release uses a aspect ratio.

On September 22, 2020, the film was once again re-released on DVD (under catalog number 2130817) in the United States by following ' 49% acquisition of Miramax. Similar to the Echo Bridge and Lionsgate releases, this release does not include any special features or subtitles and is presented in aspect ratio. This release however does not falsely advertise or imply that special features or subtitles were included, unlike the previous re-releases. 

 

===Lucario and the Mystery of Mew===
Lucario and the Mystery of Mew was released by on DVD in the United States.

The Collector's Edition DVD set was released in the United States on September 19, 2006 . This release uses a 4:3 . This set includes two discs, one containing the movie and the other containing the second dub of The Mastermind of Mirage Pokémon. The promotional card was included in early releases of the Collector's Edition DVD. Both discs include English closed captioning. The following extras are included:
A letter from the director (The Mastermind of Mirage Pokémon disc)
Behind the scenes (Lucario and the Mystery of Mew disc)
Slideshow of the characters (Lucario and the Mystery of Mew disc)
Pokémon online weblinks (Pokémon.com, Pokémon Mobile and Pokémon Learning League) on both discs

The Standard Edition DVD was released in the United States on September 24, 2013 with distribution handled through . The Standard Edition does not include The Mastermind of Mirage Pokémon. This release uses a 4:3 . The following extras are included:
Behind the scenes
Slideshow of the characters

 

===Pokémon Ranger and the Temple of the Sea===
Pokémon Ranger and the Temple of the Sea was released by on DVD in the United States.

This DVD was released in the United States on April 3, 2007 . This set includes two discs, one containing the movie and the other containing Pikachu's Island Adventure. Both discs include English closed captioning. This release uses a 16:9 . The DVD release includes the following extras:
Location scouting
Art slideshow of the characters
Interactive
Pokémon online weblinks (Pokémon.com, Pokémon Mobile, and Pokémon Learning League)

On , in addition to the standard version, a three disc version was also released on the same day. The three disc version additionally contains the disc from the first volume of the Advanced Battle season "Gaining Groudon", which contains the episodes Clamperl of Wisdom, The Relicanth Really Can, The Evolutionary War, Training Wrecks, and Gaining Groudon. Otherwise, the packaging and contents are identical to the standard version.

 

===The Rise of Darkrai===
The Rise of Darkrai was released by on DVD in the United States. It was released in the United States on May 27, 2008 . This release uses a 16:9 .

 

===Giratina and the Sky Warrior===
 
Giratina and the Sky Warrior was released in the United States by on March 31, 2009 . This release uses a .

It was re-released in the United States on July 7, 2015, with a different cover. It was released by with distribution through . It's catalogue number is 3000063725. This release uses a .

 

===Arceus and the Jewel of Life===
Arceus and the Jewel of Life was released by with distribution through on DVD in the United States. It was released in the United States on February 1, 2011 . This release uses a 16:9 .

 

===Zoroark: Master of Illusions===
Zoroark: Master of Illusions was released by with distribution through on DVD in the United States. It was released in the United States on September 20, 2011 . This release uses a . The promotional card was included in early releases of the DVD.

 

===White—Victini and Zekrom and Black—Victini and Reshiram===
White—Victini and Zekrom and Black—Victini and Reshiram have only been released in a bundle.

===Kyurem VS. The Sword of Justice===
Kyurem VS. The Sword of Justice was released by with distribution through on DVD in the United States. It was released in the United States on April 2, 2013 . This release uses a 16:9 .

 

===Genesect and The Legend Awakened===
Genesect and The Legend Awakened was released by with distribution through on DVD in the United States. It was released in the United States on December 3, 2013 . This release uses a , and includes subtitles. The promotional card was included in early releases of the DVD. The DVD release also includes a theatrical trailer for the movie.

 

===Diancie and the Cocoon of Destruction===
 
Diancie and the Cocoon of Destruction was released by with distribution through on DVD in the United States. It was released in the United States on February 17, 2015 with the catalogue number 3000058895. This release uses a . This release also includes the short Diancie — Princess of the Diamond Domain as well as a trailer.

 

===Hoopa and the Clash of Ages===
Hoopa and the Clash of Ages was released by with distribution through on DVD in the United States. It was released in the United States on March 8, 2016 with the catalogue number 3000066467. This release uses a . This release also includes a trailer and the short Hoopa — The Mischief Pokémon.

 

===Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel===
Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel was released by with distribution through on DVD in the United States. It was released in the United States on March 21, 2017 with the catalogue number 3000071587. This release uses a .

 

===I Choose You!===
 
I Choose You! was released by with distribution through in the United States.It was released February 13, 2018 on DVD with the catalogue number 3000075995 and on Blu-Ray with the catalogue number 3000075997. Both releases use a , and include English subtitles.

 

===The Power of Us===
 
The Power of Us was released by with distribution through on DVD in the United States. It was released on DVD and Blu-Ray on March 19, 2019. Both releases use a , and include English subtitles.

===Mewtwo Strikes Back—Evolution===
 
Mewtwo Strikes Back—Evolution was released by with distribution through on DVD in the United States. It was released on DVD and Blu-Ray on November 17, 2020. Both releases use a , and include English subtitles.

===Secrets of the Jungle===
 
Secrets of the Jungle was released by with distribution through on DVD in the United States. It was released on October 4, 2022 on DVD and Blu-Ray. Both releases use a , and include English subtitles.

==Multi-movie releases==
===Pokémon: The First Three Movies===
Pokémon: The First Three Movies is a multi-movie DVD set released by in the United States on April 7, 2009 with the catalogue number 300021792. It contains two discs, with Disc 2 being double-sided. The set includes Mewtwo Strikes Back, The Power of One, and Spell of the Unown: Entei. This release uses a 4:3 . The DVDs are exactly the same as the original DVDs released by Warner Bros.

The Disc 1 contains the movie Mewtwo Strikes Back and the Pikachu short Pikachu's Vacation. The DVD has English audio, with optional English and French closed captions. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Commentary audio track by Director Michael Haigney and Producer Norman J. Grossfeld
The Story of Mewtwo's Origin (first two minutes of The Uncut Story of Mewtwo's Origin)
Music video for 's " " (the movie's ending theme)
Theatrical trailer of the movie
Preview of The Power of One
"Ash's journey"
DVD-ROM features: Pokémon fun facts, history of , history of the video games, Pokémon Web World, Nintendo game guides, special events page, Pokémon webcards, Poké-patterns, Pokémon posters and more

The Disc 2 Side A contains the movie The Power of One and the Pikachu short Pikachu's Rescue Adventure. The DVD has English and Quebec French audio, and English and French closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Musical performances from the Pokémon the Movie 2000 soundtrack
"They Don't Understand" by 
"Story Of" and performance by Alysha Antonino
"Pokémon World" by featuring 
Making of the soundtrack
Theatrical trailer of the movie
Theatrical trailer of Spell of the Unown: Entei

The Disc 2 Side B contains the movie Spell of the Unown: Entei and the Pikachu short Pikachu & Pichu. The DVD has English and French audio, and English and French closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:
Pokérap GS (Johto Pokérap)
Making of "To Know the Unknown"
What the Filmmakers Say (Commentary audio track)
Theatrical trailer of the movie
Japanese trailer for Celebi: The Voice of the Forest
Little Known Unown Facts!

 

===Pokémon 4Ever / Pokémon Heroes - Double Feature===
 
The Pokémon 4Ever / Pokémon Heroes - Double Feature DVD was released by with distribution through in the United States. It was released on April 19, 2011. It contains one double-sided disc, with Pokémon 4Ever - Celebi: The Voice of the Forest on one side and Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias on the other. 

It does not includes Pikachu shorts or other special features from the original individual DVD releases of the movies.

 

===Pokémon Heroes / Destiny Deoxys - Double Feature===
The Pokémon Heroes / Destiny Deoxys - Double Feature Blu-ray was released by and distributed by in the United States. It was released on May 15, 2011. It contains one disc, which contains both Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias and Destiny Deoxys. This release uses a .

It does not include Pikachu shorts or other special features from the original individual DVD releases of the movies.

 

===Destiny Deoxys / Jirachi: Wish Maker - Double Feature===
 
The Destiny Deoxys / Jirachi: Wish Maker - Double Feature DVD was released by and distributed by in the United States. It was released on October 4, 2011. It contains one disc that contains both Destiny Deoxys and Jirachi: Wish Maker. 

It does not includes Pikachu shorts or other special features from the original individual DVD releases of the movies.

 

===Pokémon Collector's Set DVD===
The Pokémon Collector's Set is a multi-movie DVD set released by in the United States. It contains four movies on one disc: Celebi: The Voice of the Forest, Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias, Jirachi: Wish Maker, and Destiny Deoxys. It has been re-released several times with different covers by different distributors. This set does not include Pikachu shorts, other special features, or subtitles in any of its releases.

It was released in the United States on June 7, 2011 distributed by under the titles "Pokémon Collector's Set" and "Pokémon Collector's Series" with the catalogue number 78949. The disc is two sided, with Celebi: The Voice of the Forest and Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias on Side A, and Jirachi: Wish Maker and Destiny Deoxys on Side B. These releases use a 4:3 .

It was re-released in the United States on December 3, 2013, distributed by as the "Pokémon Limited Edition Collector's Set" with the catalogue number 23424. The set contains a single one-sided disc. This release uses a aspect ratio.

It was re-released again on DVD in the United States on March 3, 2015, distributed by under the titles "Pokémon Collector's Set: 4 Films" and "Pokémon Collector's Set: 4 Movies". The set contains a single one-sided disc. These releases use a aspect ratio.

On September 22, 2020, the set was re-released and labeled under titles "Pokémon Collector's Set: 4 Movies" and "Pokemon 4 Movie Collection" (under catalog number 2130688) in the United States by and was distributed by following ' 49% acquisition of Miramax. Similar to the Echo Bridge and Lionsgate re-releases, the set contained a single DVD disc and are presented in aspect ratio. 

 

===Pokémon Collector's Set Blu-ray===
The Pokémon Collector's Set is a multi-movie Blu-ray set released in the United States on April 3, 2012 under the titles "Miramax Multi-Feature" and "Pokémon Collector's Set". It was released by and distributed by . It contains four movies on one disc: Celebi: The Voice of the Forest, Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias, Jirachi: Wish Maker, and Destiny Deoxys. This set uses a .

This set does not include Pikachu shorts or other special features.

 

===Pokémon the Movie: Black—Victini and Reshiram / White—Victini and Zekrom===
 
Pokémon the Movie: Black—Victini and Reshiram / White—Victini and Zekrom is a multi-movie DVD set released in the United States on April 3, 2012. It was released by with distribution through . It contains two discs, one with Black—Victini and Reshiram and the other with White—Victini and Zekrom. This set uses a for both films. It also includes trailers for both films.

 

===5 Kids Action Movies===
 
The 5 Kids Action Movies DVD set is a multi-movie DVD set released in the United States on September 3, 2013. It was released by and distributed by . It contains five movies on two discs: Celebi: The Voice of the Forest, Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias, Jirachi: Wish Maker, , and Destiny Deoxys. 

This set does not include Pikachu shorts or other special features.

 

===Pokémon: The Movies 1-3 Collection===
The Pokémon: The Movies 1-3 Collection is a multi-movie Blu-ray set released by with distribution through . The Limited Edition Steelbook contains three discs, with one movie on each, while the standard and DVD releases only contain one disc with all three movies on it. It includes Mewtwo Strikes Back, The Power of One, and Spell of the Unown: Entei. This set uses a .

It was released in a Limited Edition Steelbook case in the United States on February 9, 2016 with the catalogue number 3000066501. Optional English closed captioning is not included.

It was released in a standard case in the United States on October 2, 2018 with the catalogue number 3000079069. Optional English closed captioning is included.

A DVD version of the set was released on April 9th, 2019 with the catalogue number 1000742791. Optional English closed captioning is included

 

===Pokémon Diamond & Pearl 4-Movie Collection===
The Pokémon Diamond & Pearl 4-Movie Collection is a multi-movie Blu-ray set released in the United States on December 6, 2016 with the catalogue number 3000064687. It was released by with distribution through . It contains four discs, with one movie on each. It includes The Rise of Darkrai, Giratina and the Sky Warrior, Arceus and the Jewel of Life, and Zoroark: Master of Illusions. Optional English closed captioning is included. This set uses a .

 

=== Pokémon Black & White 4-Movie Collection ===
The Pokémon Black & White 4-Movie Collection is a multi-movie Blu-ray set released in the United States on September 17, 2019 with the catalogue number 3000081403. It was released by VIZ Media with distribution through Warner Home Video. It contains two discs, with two movies on each. It includes White—Victini and Zekrom, Black—Victini and Reshiram, Kyurem VS. The Sword of Justice and Genesect and The Legend Awakened. Optional English closed captioning is included. This set uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.
 

===Pokémon XY Mega 3-Movie Collection===
 
The Pokémon XY Mega 3-Movie Collection is a multi-movie DVD and Blu-ray set that was released in the United States on October 17, 2023 by with distribution through . The DVD contains two discs, while the Blu-Ray contains one disc with all three movies on it. The set includes Diancie & the Cocoon of Destruction, Hoopa & the Clash of Ages and Volcanion & the Mechanical Marvel. Optional English closed captioning is included. This set uses a .

 

===Pokémon Double Feature: The First Movie / I Choose You!===
Pokémon Double Feature: The First Movie / I Choose You! is a multi-movie DVD and Blu-ray set released by with distribution through . It contains two discs, with one movie on each. It includes Mewtwo Strikes Back and I Choose You!. This set uses a .

It was released in the United States on November 16, 2021 with the catalogue number 3000087395 (Blu Ray) and 30000087397 (DVD).

 

=== Pokémon: Tales of Lugia ===
Pokémon: Tales of Lugia is a multi-movie DVD released in the United States on February 27, 2024 with the catalogue number 3000097310. It was released by VIZ Media with distribution through Warner Home Video. It includes Pokémon the Movie 2000, and Pokémon the Movie: The Power of Us, both on one disc. This set uses a 16:9 aspect ratio.

sections.heading: Celebi: The Voice of the Forest
sections.text:

It was released on VHS in the United States on March 18, 2003 with the catalogue number 29173. It was released on DVD in the United States by on March 18, 2003 with the catalogue number 29124. It was released on DVD in Canada by Alliance Atlantis with the catalogue number 4611. They all use a 4:3 . The DVD has English audio, with optional English closed captions. In addition to Pikachu's PikaBoo, the DVD release includes the following extras:
Audio commentary by the actors and producers,
Multi-angle animation progression on four scenes
A trivia game
A Trading Card Game tutorial as a DVD-ROM feature
Theatrical trailers (domestic and Japanese trailer)
A sneak peek at the next Pokémon movie

On September 22, 2020, the film was once again re-released on DVD (under catalog number 2130815) in the United States by following ' 49% acquisition of Miramax. The set includes Mewtwo Strikes Back, The Power of One, and Spell of the Unown: Entei. This release uses a 4:3 . The DVDs are exactly the same as the original DVDs released by Warner Bros.

The Disc 1 contains the movie Mewtwo Strikes Back and the Pikachu short Pikachu's Vacation. The DVD has English audio, with optional English and French closed captions. The DVD release includes the following extras:

Music video for 's " " (the movie's ending theme)
Theatrical trailer of the movie

DVD-ROM features: Pokémon fun facts, history of , history of the video games, Pokémon Web World, Nintendo game guides, special events page, Pokémon webcards, Poké-patterns, Pokémon posters and more

The Disc 2 Side A contains the movie The Power of One and the Pikachu short Pikachu's Rescue Adventure. The DVD has English and Quebec French audio, and English and French closed captioning. The DVD release includes the following extras:

sections.heading: Pokémon Collector's Set DVD
sections.text:
The Pokémon Collector's Set is a multi-movie DVD set released by in the United States. It contains four movies on one disc: Celebi: The Voice of the Forest, Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias, Jirachi: Wish Maker, and Destiny Deoxys. It has been re-released several times with different covers by different distributors. This set does not include Pikachu shorts, other special features, or subtitles in any of its releases.

It was released in the United States on June 7, 2011 distributed by under the titles "Pokémon Collector's Set" and "Pokémon Collector's Series" with the catalogue number 78949. The disc is two sided, with Celebi: The Voice of the Forest and Pokémon Heroes: Latios & Latias on Side A, and Jirachi: Wish Maker and Destiny Deoxys on Side B. These releases use a 4:3 .

It was re-released in the United States on December 3, 2013, distributed by as the "Pokémon Limited Edition Collector's Set" with the catalogue number 23424. The set contains a single one-sided disc. This release uses a aspect ratio.

It was re-released again on DVD in the United States on March 3, 2015, distributed by under the titles "Pokémon Collector's Set: 4 Films" and "Pokémon Collector's Set: 4 Movies". The set contains a single one-sided disc. These releases use a aspect ratio.

On September 22, 2020, the set was re-released and labeled under titles "Pokémon Collector's Set: 4 Movies" and "Pokemon 4 Movie Collection" (under catalog number 2130688) in the United States by and was distributed by following ' 49% acquisition of Miramax. Similar to the Echo Bridge and Lionsgate re-releases, the set contained a single DVD disc and are presented in aspect ratio.

It includes The Rise of Darkrai, Giratina and the Sky Warrior, Arceus and the Jewel of Life, and Zoroark: Master of Illusions. Optional English closed captioning is included. This set uses a .
